searchText: <@552133098075193354> I made a [comment](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/all-core-devs-execution-acde-203-january-16-2025/22346/5?u=claravanstaden) on the ACD page (but perhaps it is not the right place). Would really appreciate at least a month's lead time on the mainnet epoch for the Electra upgrade. 🙏 Thanks for sharing! We can discuss this on the call, but my sense from talking to others in the community is that they'd like to see the fork happen ASAP. Assuming we fork testnets in ~mid Feb, there would likely be ~1 month between that and the mainnet fork, but it's unlikely to be 1 month from the last testnet forking to mainnet (maybe 2-3 weeks?), which is when we'd probably set the epoch. And you couldn't perhaps set a tentative epoch now (pending successful devnet 6, Holesky and Sepolia)? Please no. Setting Holesky/Sepolia was already a stretch. One of the ELs is still not functioning at all on devnet-5 Find out first if they work Once the "tentative" date is out there, it has a self-perpetuating quality and in general devnet-5 only regained finality today What's the value you get from having the exact epoch longer in advance? For example, if we said "be ready for ~mid march" vs. "we'll fork on $EPOCH (that lands on March 15)"? I need to set the correct epoch so that our Ethereum light client knows how to handle headers: https://github.com/polkadot-fellows/runtimes/blob/main/system-parachains/bridge-hubs/bridge-hub-polkadot/src/bridge_to_ethereum_config.rs#L117 To lay out the process: 1. Update the epoch in the code linked above, get the PR merged and the new Polkadot runtime released. 2. Create a referendum for the Polkadot community to vote on the upgrade, e.g. https://polkadot.polkassembly.io/referenda/1202?tab=description 3. The community votes on the referendum, can take 2-3 weeks. On successful voting, the upgrade executes. I realize this might be a unique request and that most of the community might want an earlier upgrade, but I'd ask at least 3 weeks notice if at all possible. 🙂 If the Electra epoch changes, the referendum could just be cancelled. We would typically want at least 3 weeks to distribute the message that the upgrade is happening so validators don't get caught out, so I do believe we're fairly aligned in that desire for notice... I think it's becoming clear by the minute that yes, the community wants the fork ASAP but it's practically impossible to ship this with less than a month notice from the public testnet launches. Doing mainnet releases right after the testnets with two weeks notice and having to roll those back with less than a week notice if there's something wrong in the testnet is just crazy. Let alone big node operators have their own slow procedures for upgrading My position is that I don't deeply care about the exact time interval between these things, but I want: - `devnet-5` to work, reliably, with all the CLs and ELs; - `devnet-6` to work, reliably, with all the CLs and ELs; and - Holesky to work, reliably, with all the CLs and ELs before committing to a mainnet fork epoch. I think it is a very reasonable note that if we expect L2s (and other apps) to have things like enforced upgrade delays and strong governance, L1 upgrades are going to have to give enough notice to let those processes play out.

excerpts.author: claravanstaden
excerpts.content:
I need to set the correct epoch so that our Ethereum light client knows how to handle headers: https://github.com/polkadot-fellows/runtimes/blob/main/system-parachains/bridge-hubs/bridge-hub-polkadot/src/bridge_to_ethereum_config.rs#L117

To lay out the process:
1. Update the epoch in the code linked above, get the PR merged and the new Polkadot runtime released.
2. Create a referendum for the Polkadot community to vote on the upgrade, e.g. https://polkadot.polkassembly.io/referenda/1202?tab=description
3. The community votes on the referendum, can take 2-3 weeks. On successful voting, the upgrade executes.

I realize this might be a unique request and that most of the community might want an earlier upgrade, but I'd ask at least 3 weeks notice if at all possible. 🙂
